issues.legal_issue: A legislature may retrospectively validate municipal property-tax assessments made under a doubtful or defective authority where the validation is constitutionally permissible and the taxing measure has not already been declared invalid.
material_facts: The municipality continued property-tax assessments using the method prescribed by a government order after the earlier municipal statute had been repealed.
A later amendment expressly validated municipal actions taken to continue the levy and collection of property tax using that method, notwithstanding the governing statute or transitional orders.
The amendment also amended the provisions governing the basis for property-tax assessment.
The validity of the validating provision was not challenged, and no court had declared the tax measure invalid before the amendment.
issues.conclusion: The amendment validly validated the municipal actions and the resulting levy and collection; the challenge to them therefore failed.
issues.legal_principle: The legislative power to tax is sovereign and must be exercised within constitutional limits. Within those limits, a legislature may retrospectively regularise an irregular assessment and validate a taxing measure of doubtful validity where a court has not already declared it invalid. A statute is not declared unconstitutional unless specifically challenged. The Court distinguished Janapada Sabha Chhindwara v. The Central Provinces Syndicate Ltd., [1970] 3 SCR 745, where the validating enactment did not sufficiently amend the law and attempted to affect a court decision, and applied the rule in Shamarao V. Parulekar v. The District Magistrate, Thana, [1952] 3 SCR 683, that an amendment is read into the amended Act unless that produces inconsistency.

rule.if: municipal_tax_appeal and legislature_enacted_clear_retroactive_validation and not prior_judgment_invalidated_tax_measure and not validation_law_challenged

predicates.municipal_tax_appeal: The proceeding challenges municipal property-tax assessments or their levy and collection.
predicates.legislature_enacted_clear_retroactive_va: The legislature enacted a measure that clearly validates the relevant municipal tax actions retrospectively.
predicates.prior_judgment_invalidated_tax_measure: A court had already declared the relevant taxing measure invalid before the validating measure was enacted.
predicates.validation_law_challenged: The challenger specifically contested the validity of the validating law.

issues.definition: When a municipal-tax appeal concerns actions clearly validated retrospectively, and no court had already invalidated the measure and the validation law is not challenged, the retrospective validation is effective.

issues.legal_issue: A government order prescribing a repealed statute’s assessment method as a transitional measure does not revive that statute, and actions taken under the order can be validated as actions taken pursuant to the order.
material_facts: The earlier municipal statute had been repealed by the later municipal statute.
A transitional provision permitted the government to direct how municipal taxes were to be levied.

The government issued an order directing the municipality to continue using the assessment method found in the repealed statute, and that order covered the period after repeal up to the commencement of the validating amendment.
The validating amendment covered municipal actions taken pursuant to the government order.
issues.conclusion: The government order did not revive the repealed statute; it prescribed the former assessment method as a transitional measure, and the relevant municipal actions were validated as actions taken pursuant to that order.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 389 and 391 of the Andhra Pradesh Municipalities Act, 1965, read with Schedule IX, Rule 12, the transitional tax arrangements operated subject to government directions. The validating provision in Section 4(1) of the Andhra Pradesh Municipalities (Fourth Amendment) Act, 1975, validated actions taken pursuant to the relevant government order. The order’s reference to the repealed statute prescribed its method without reviving it; there was no gap in the covered period. The amendment must be read into the principal Act consistently with Shamarao V. Parulekar v. The District Magistrate, Thana, [1952] 3 SCR 683.

predicates.municipal_tax_appeal: The proceeding challenges municipal property-tax assessments or their levy and collection.
predicates.prior_tax_law_repealed: The statute that previously governed the tax method had been repealed before the disputed assessments.
predicates.government_order_prescribed_its_method_t: The government directed the municipality to use the former method as a transitional arrangement without making the repealed statute itself operative.
predicates.legislative_validation_covers_order_base: A legislative measure retrospectively validated the municipal actions taken pursuant to the government order.

issues.definition: In a municipal-tax appeal, when the former law has been repealed, a government order prescribes its method transitionally, and legislation validates actions under that order, the former law is not revived and the covered actions are validated.
